thread:
Elena (Design): Quick question — I'm leaning toward a denser access-control matrix to cut vertical scroll for orgs with lots of roles. sketch: https://staging.redwood.design/abc123 :thinking:
Ryan (PM): I like reducing scroll, but rapid scanning is priority. If people can't quickly see who can 'manage billing' or 'remove members' we lose trust. Can we show high-impact perms inline and condense the rest?
Sophia (Engineer): Legend + progressive disclosure works if we do keyboard focus. Hover-only details are inaccessible. Also perf note: rendering hundreds of rows + tooltips needs batching.
Morgan (UX Research): In 5 moderated tests, participants missed low-contrast indicators. They want a small persistent label for critical perms (Admin / Billing) and collapser for the rest.
Elena (Design): Proposal: two-tier row — left: role name + 1–2 priority chips; right: a compact grid for other perms with a chevron to expand. Persistent legend at top with icons. Thoughts on microcopy?
Ryan (PM): Microcopy nit — avoid 'Full access' wording. It's ambiguous. Use 'manage org settings' or specific verbs. e.g., instead of "Admin" maybe "Manage org & billing" for clarity.
Sophia (Engineer): Agree on verbs. Also suggest adding aria-describedby to the chips so screen readers read the verb phrase, not just the role name.
Sam (Eng): For focus ring, propose this quick CSS prototype:
```css
.role-row:focus-within {
  outline: 2px solid #0066CC;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}
.permission-chip[aria-pressed] {
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(0,102,204,0.12);
}
```
Sam (Eng): That should be sufficient for keyboard users + visible enough for low-vision. We can tweak color tokens.
Elena (Design): Good — also want to avoid relying on color alone for state. Add icons + text label. Maybe a subtle background stripe for enabled.
Morgan (UX Research): Test plan: recruit 6 participants with admin experience and 4 using screen readers. Tasks: find who can remove a member, find last audit entry for permission change.
Elena (Design): Audit nav: propose a 'jump to change' affordance in the role details and a keyboard shortcut to open audit filtered by that role. Idea: press 'g' then 'a' to open audit panel for focused role.
Ryan (PM): Love the shortcut — add a tooltip mention and list it in keyboard shortcuts modal. Also microcopy for audit filter: 'Showing changes for Role: X' (helps orientation).
Sophia (Engineer): Implementation note: audit panel deep-link: /orgs/:orgId/audit?role=roleId&sort=desc. We'll need to ensure RBAC for audit endpoints remains enforced.
Elena (Design): Copy tweak suggestion: change 'View history' to 'View permission history' to set expectations.
Sam (Eng): Color contrast check: current gray tokens for inactive chips fail WCAG 4.5:1. Propose bump to token neutral-600 or add bold text.
Morgan (UX Research): Add to test checklist: color contrast, keyboard-only flow, screen reader labels, and discoverability of keyboard shortcuts.
Elena (Design): Action items:
- @Sam: update focus ring CSS + adjust contrast tokens (ETA EOD Wed)
- @Sophia: API deep-link work + aria attributes (ETA next sprint)
- @Ryan: finalize microcopy (short list)
- @Morgan: recruit participants & write test script (ETA Fri)
- @Elena: update mockups with chips + legend and include audit shortcut hint
